description: MoonBase Mission Trainer is a short pitch deck from team Lunar Crew for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It proposes a game where students run a Moon base. They manage power, oxygen, water, food and radiation, react to events like dust storms, and see how each choice affects the crew. The goal is to teach systems thinking and decision-making in a safe, hands-on way.
summary:
MoonBase Mission Trainer is a proposed interactive simulation for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Challenge 03). Students act as commander of a lunar outpost and learn how space missions work by making resource trade-offs.
The problem: Running a Moon base means balancing power, oxygen, water and food, and all of them depend on each other. Young learners rarely get a safe, accessible way to experiment with those trade-offs and see the consequences.
The idea: Students command the outpost, respond to events and adapt as conditions change. Each round follows a loop: receive resources, make decisions, simulate the changes, evaluate crew safety, then reach success or failure and continue or reset. The simulation tracks five systems: power, life support (oxygen and water), food, radiation shielding and overall mission state. A dashboard shows resource levels with an incoming event and four choices: Conserve, Deploy, Shield and Prioritize.
The build: The plan is a Streamlit web interface on top of a simple Python simulation that uses intentionally simplified calculations. The slides stress that planned features aren't presented as implemented, and that NASA open data and credible scientific references will be used where relevant.
details:
Project name: MoonBase Mission Trainer

Event: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Challenge 03

Team: Lunar Crew (Nanda Raghunath, Raniya A.H, S Anupama, Megha K)

One-line summary: An interactive lunar outpost survival simulation.

Target users: Young learners and students.

Problem: Mission planning involves linked systems, uncertainty and long chains of consequences, and students rarely get an accessible, hands-on way to explore those trade-offs.

Solution: Students play mission commander. They allocate resources, react to events and keep the outpost running as conditions change.

Core mechanics:

Systems: Power, life support (oxygen and water), food, radiation shielding and mission state.

Loop: Start, receive resources, make decisions, simulate resource changes, evaluate crew safety, then success or failure, and continue or reset.

Dashboard: Resource bars (for example Power 72%, Oxygen 88%, Water 61%, Food 76% on Sol 18), an event panel, and four actions: Conserve, Deploy, Shield, Prioritize.

Tech stack: Streamlit for the interface, a Python simulation for resource rules and conditional outcomes, and a simplified learning model for the calculations.

Data and references: NASA open data and credible scientific references where relevant. The deck doesn't name specific datasets.

Status: The dashboard and architecture are labeled as a prototype concept and a proposed build, not finished features.

Learning outcomes: Visible resource management, systems thinking, safe testing of engineering trade-offs, and links between space exploration and decision-making, teamwork and curiosity.
